request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; active_leak for water visibly dripping or running
  from a pipe, hose or fitting; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: white upper wall cabinets with black pulls
range hood space with no appliances
exposed plumbing where base cabinets and sink were removed

damaged_parts.condition: drywall and insulation stripped to the studs; wood dark and stained, with possible mould growth up to a consistent height
removed or missing, leaving upper cabinets hanging above bare framing
tile section visible; surrounding floor covered in dark residue, with debris and sediment
pipes, drain traps and wall outlets exposed; some corrosion and staining visible, with wiring hanging loose

materials: black iron or ABS drain pipe
visible_items: toilet visible through an opening in the stripped wall
regional_indicators: North American style duplex electrical outlets
US style cabinetry and framing with timber studs
parsed_output.summary_en: A gutted kitchen with the lower walls stripped to bare, dark-stained studs, base cabinets removed and plumbing and outlets exposed, while the upper cabinets remain intact. The consistent height of the stripping, dark staining and residue on the floor suggest earlier water or flood damage, and a toilet is visible in the adjoining space.
